title: Peter Zeihan: The Iran War Could Reshape the Global Economy | Prof G Conversations
channel: The Prof G Pod – Scott Galloway
summary: Peter Zeihan, ten days into the 2026 US-Israeli war on Iran, says Hormuz is shut, a recession is locked in, Iran will now race for a bomb and Russia never negotiates.

assertions.quote: this is the first time that the Strait of Hormuz has ever been blocked. Uh we're looking at a 98% reduction in traffic
there's already enough damage to cause a global energy induced recession even if this stops right now.

verdicts.note: Whether the 2026 oil shock tipped the world into recession is not established in the evidence at hand.

assertions.quote: obviously the Iranians think they need to nuke now because it's their only option.
if you declare victory and go home, they will have a nuclear weapon within a year if they're really slow about it.

verdicts.note: Strikes in 2025 and 2026 destroyed much of Iran's enrichment and weapons infrastructure; a bomb within a year is possible but not the expected case.

assertions.quote: one PAC-3 missile costs $4 million. One Shahed costs 40 to 50,000 dollars.

verdicts.note: Interceptors cost tens to hundreds of times more than Shahed-type drones and are produced far more slowly, a cost-exchange problem seen in Ukraine and the Gulf.

US intelligence expects adversaries to pair high-end missiles with cheaper expendable systems specifically to stress US missile defences, which supports the mechanism without measuring interceptor depletion.

assertions.quote: not once in Russian history have the Russians ever negotiated an end to a conflict unless they had already won or already lost

verdicts.note: Russia has accepted negotiated stalemates, such as the 1996 Khasavyurt accord in Chechnya and the 1940 Moscow Peace that ended the Winter War short of its aims.

For Ukraine, DDIS judges Russia will agree to a ceasefire only if most demands are met or the war's costs outweigh its benefits; a cost-driven settlement short of victory is allowed for, and it is not a general rule.

assertions.quote: they have to reach the Danube, the Carpathians, the Vistula, and the Baltic, and they will not stop until they get there

verdicts.note: That line runs through NATO territory, and forecasters put a Russian attack on NATO well under even odds; Russia's stated war aims centre on Ukraine.
